principle: Every label names a structure prototype, never a chemical class (Oxide, Telluride) and never a specific compound (Bi2Te3, PbTe). Bi2Te3 and Sb2Te3 are both tetradymite; PbTe, SnTe and AgSbTe2 are all rocksalt; BiCuSeO and LaFeAsO are both ZrCuSiAs-type. This is the single-axis fix for the current MaterialFamily list, which mixes all three axes.
mp_id_policy: null until resolved against the Materials Project API in stage 2. Do not fill these in by hand or from memory.

fields.id: stable snake_case key used in annotations and by_family/ filenames
fields.name: human-readable prototype name
fields.space_group: space group of the prototype (aristotype where a distortion series exists)
fields.chemistry_class: informational second axis, for navigation only -- never the label itself
fields.aliases: current MaterialFamily values and common names that map here
fields.mp_id: Materials Project id of the prototype structure, filled in stage 2

prototypes.name: Tetradymite (Bi2Te3-type)
prototypes.notes: Quintuple-layer van der Waals chalcogenide. Covers the whole (Bi,Sb)2(Te,Se)3 solid solution.

prototypes.name: Rocksalt (NaCl-type)
prototypes.notes: PbTe, PbSe, PbS, SnTe and their solid solutions. Also disordered AgSbTe2 and cubic TAGS. Cubic GeTe above ~700 K belongs here; use gete_rhombohedral for the room-temperature phase.

prototypes.name: Rhombohedral GeTe
prototypes.notes: Ferroelectric rhombohedral distortion of rocksalt, stable below ~700 K.

prototypes.name: Layered GeS-type (SnSe)
prototypes.notes: Orthorhombic layered IV-VI. SnSe, SnS, GeSe. Distinct from rocksalt SnTe.

prototypes.name: Stibnite (Bi2S3-type)
prototypes.notes: Bi2S3, Sb2Se3, Sb2S3. Ribbon-like, not layered like tetradymite.

prototypes.name: Superionic Cu2Se
prototypes.notes: Antifluorite-like Se sublattice with liquid-like Cu. Low-T phase is a complex monoclinic superstructure; annotate the phase actually measured when the paper says.

prototypes.name: Naumannite (Ag2Se)
prototypes.notes: Orthorhombic below ~406 K, bcc superionic above.

prototypes.name: Tetrahedrite
prototypes.notes: Includes tennantite (As) and the Zn/Fe/Ni-substituted natural series.

prototypes.name: Chalcopyrite
prototypes.notes: Ordered zincblende superstructure. CuFeS2, CuInSe2, CuGaTe2, CuInTe2.

prototypes.name: Stannite / kesterite
prototypes.notes: Quaternary diamond-like. Stannite and kesterite differ only in cation ordering; record which if the paper states it.

prototypes.name: Famatinite (Cu3SbSe4-type)
prototypes.notes: Also Cu3SbS4. Cu3SbSe3 is a different, orthorhombic (Pnma) structure.

prototypes.name: Argyrodite
prototypes.notes: Cu/Ag superionic conductors, Cu7PSe6, Ag9GaSe6.

prototypes.name: CdI2-type layered dichalcogenide
prototypes.notes: 1T TiS2, NbSe2, intercalated MxTiS2. Use for 1T; note 2H polytype (P63/mmc) separately if stated.

prototypes.name: ZrCuSiAs-type (1111)
prototypes.notes: Alternating oxide and chalcogenide/pnictide layers. Covers BiCuSeO and LaFeAsO alike -- the clearest case where prototype beats chemistry class.

prototypes.name: Bi2O2Se-type
prototypes.notes: Bi2O2 fluorite-like layers alternating with Se. Related to but distinct from ZrCuSiAs.

prototypes.name: Layered In2Se3 / InSe
prototypes.notes: Many polytypes (alpha, beta, gamma). Record the polytype when stated.

prototypes.name: Sphalerite (zincblende)
prototypes.notes: Binary tetrahedral semiconductors: ZnTe, CdTe, GaAs, InSb.

prototypes.name: Wurtzite
prototypes.notes: ZnO and Al/Ga-doped ZnO, CdS, GaN.

prototypes.name: Skutterudite
prototypes.notes: Binary CoSb3 and filled RxCo4Sb12 / RFe4Sb12. Fillers are guest atoms in the icosahedral void -- record them as fillers, not substitutional dopants, in stage 3.

prototypes.name: Half-Heusler (MgAgAs-type, C1b)
prototypes.notes: XYZ 1:1:1. TiNiSn, ZrNiSn, NbFeSb, TaFeSb, TiCoSb. Half of the Heusler cube's tetrahedral sites are vacant.

prototypes.name: Full Heusler (Cu2MnAl-type, L21)
prototypes.notes: X2YZ 2:1:1. Fe2VAl, Fe2TiSn.

prototypes.name: Clathrate type I
prototypes.notes: Ba8Ga16Ge30, Ba8Ga16Sn30, Ba8AlxSi46, Ba8Cu6Si40. Guest atoms in dodecahedral/tetrakaidecahedral cages.

prototypes.name: Clathrate type II
prototypes.notes: Larger hexakaidecahedral cages, often partially filled.

prototypes.name: beta-Zn4Sb3
prototypes.notes: Disordered interstitial Zn. Distinct from ZnSb -- check stoichiometry.

prototypes.name: CdSb-type (ZnSb)
prototypes.notes: 1:1 ZnSb and CdSb, not to be confused with beta-Zn4Sb3.

prototypes.name: CaAl2Si2-type Zintl (1-2-2)
prototypes.notes: Mg3Sb2, Mg3Bi2, CaZn2Sb2, YbZn2Sb2 and the Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 solid solution.

prototypes.name: Yb14MnSb11-type Zintl (14-1-11)
prototypes.notes: Also Ca14AlSb11. Very large unit cell.

prototypes.name: ThCr2Si2-type (122)
prototypes.notes: Layered 122 intermetallics and pnictides.

prototypes.name: Antifluorite (Mg2Si-type)
prototypes.notes: Mg2Si, Mg2Ge, Mg2Sn and the full Mg2(Si,Sn) solid solution.

prototypes.name: Nowotny chimney-ladder (higher manganese silicide)
prototypes.notes: Mn4Si7, Mn11Si19, Mn15Si26, Mn27Si47. Incommensurate composite -- MP entries exist only for the commensurate approximants.

prototypes.name: beta-FeSi2
prototypes.notes: Semiconducting beta phase. The metallic alpha phase (P4/mmm) is different.

prototypes.name: CrSi2-type (C40)
prototypes.notes: CrSi2, also used for VSi2, NbSi2.

prototypes.name: B20 (FeSi-type)
prototypes.notes: Chiral cubic FeSi, CoSi, MnSi. Distinguish from beta-FeSi2 by stoichiometry.

prototypes.name: Th3P4-type
prototypes.notes: La3-xTe4 with variable cation vacancies -- the vacancy level is the carrier-concentration knob, relevant to stage 3.

prototypes.name: Chevrel phase
prototypes.notes: Mo6X8 clusters with intercalated cations.

prototypes.name: Diamond cubic
prototypes.notes: Si, Ge and the full SiGe solid solution.

prototypes.name: A7 rhombohedral (alpha-As type)
prototypes.notes: Bi, Sb, As and Bi-Sb alloys.

prototypes.name: Trigonal Te / Se
prototypes.notes: Helical chains.

prototypes.name: Silicon carbide polytypes
prototypes.notes: Record the polytype (3C/4H/6H) when the paper states it.

prototypes.name: Boron carbide / alpha-boron
prototypes.notes: Icosahedral B12 framework, wide homogeneity range B4C-B13C2.

prototypes.name: Graphite / graphene
prototypes.notes: Graphite, graphene, CNT and reduced graphene oxide. Nanocarbon morphologies share this prototype -- record morphology as a separate attribute.

prototypes.name: Quasicrystal and approximant
prototypes.notes: Al-Pd-Re, Al-Pd-Mn, Al-Cu-Fe. No periodic MP structure for the true quasicrystal; map to the nearest approximant and flag it.

prototypes.name: Disordered metallic solid solution
prototypes.notes: Use only when there is genuinely no ordered prototype. Record the lattice (fcc/bcc/hcp).

prototypes.name: Perovskite
prototypes.notes: SrTiO3, CaMnO3, LaMnO3, LaCoO3, BaTiO3, SrRuO3. Record the distortion (cubic/orthorhombic/rhombohedral) when stated. Double perovskites get their own id.

prototypes.name: Double perovskite
prototypes.notes: B-site ordered A2BB'O6.

prototypes.name: Ruddlesden-Popper / K2NiF4-type
prototypes.notes: n=1 K2NiF4 (T-type La2CuO4, La2NiO4, Sr2RuO4). Nd2CuO4 is the T'-variant -- same id, note the variant. Higher n members (Sr3Ti2O7) also belong here with n recorded.

prototypes.name: Misfit layered cobaltite
prototypes.notes: [Ca2CoO3][CoO2]_x and the Bi-Sr-Co-O, Bi-Ca-Co-O analogues. Incommensurate composite of a rocksalt block and a CdI2-type CoO2 layer -- MP has no single matching entry, so stage 2 must map the two subsystems separately.

prototypes.name: Layered NaxCoO2 (gamma-type)
prototypes.notes: CdI2-type CoO2 layers with Na between them. x is a compositional variable, not a dopant.

prototypes.name: Ca3Co2O6-type chain oxide
prototypes.notes: 1D face-sharing CoO6 chains. Frequently co-occurs with Ca3Co4O9 in the same papers -- check stoichiometry carefully.

prototypes.name: Delafossite
prototypes.notes: CuAlO2, CuCrO2, CuFeO2. Transparent p-type oxides.

prototypes.name: Rutile
prototypes.notes: TiO2 rutile, SnO2, VO2 (above the metal-insulator transition; the monoclinic M1 phase below it is a distinct structure).

prototypes.name: Anatase
prototypes.notes: Distinguish from rutile only when the paper identifies the polymorph.

prototypes.name: Magneli phase
prototypes.notes: TinO2n-1 and reduced TiO2-x. Common in oxygen-deficient titanate papers.

prototypes.name: Bixbyite (C-type sesquioxide)
prototypes.notes: In2O3, Y2O3, and Sc2O3.

prototypes.name: InGaO3(ZnO)n homologous
prototypes.notes: Natural superlattice In-Zn-O phases; n sets the layer period.

prototypes.name: Corundum
prototypes.notes: Al2O3, Fe2O3 (hematite), Cr2O3, Ti2O3.

prototypes.name: Spinel
prototypes.notes: Normal and inverse spinels, Fe3O4, ZnFe2O4, NiCo2O4.

prototypes.name: Rocksalt oxide
prototypes.notes: MgO, CdO, CoO, NiO, MnO. Same prototype as rocksalt chalcogenides but kept separate for navigability.

prototypes.name: Tenorite (CuO)
prototypes.notes: Cu2O (cuprite, Pn-3m) is a different prototype -- check the oxidation state.

prototypes.name: Fluorite oxide
prototypes.notes: CeO2, UO2, ZrO2 (cubic stabilised), and doped ionic conductors.

prototypes.name: ReO3-type / WO3
prototypes.notes: WO3 and its tilt distortions; also tungsten/molybdenum bronzes.

prototypes.name: Layered V2O5
prototypes.notes: Layered vanadium pentoxide and vanadium bronzes.

prototypes.name: YBCO-type cuprate
prototypes.notes: 123 cuprate with CuO chains; oxygen content 6+delta is the doping variable for stage 3.

prototypes.name: BSCCO-type cuprate
prototypes.notes: Bi-2201/2212/2223 homologous series; record the member.

prototypes.name: Amorphous / glassy
prototypes.notes: No periodic structure. No MP assignment possible -- stage 2 should skip these.

prototypes.name: Composite / multiphase
prototypes.notes: Deliberate two-phase or nanocomposite samples. Record the matrix prototype and the second-phase prototype separately rather than forcing one label.

prototypes.name: Organic / conducting polymer
prototypes.notes: PEDOT:PSS, polyaniline. Mostly out of scope for this TE inorganic set -- the organic project has its own table.

prototypes.name: Unresolved
prototypes.notes: Use when the host system is genuinely ambiguous or the composition string is malformed. Always give a reason.
